title: Vendor bank details changed
search_query: vendor bank account change request business email compromise payment fraud warning
how: A real vendor's email is hacked or spoofed, and a message says they've switched banks. The next invoice looks normal, but the money goes to the criminal's account. Onboarding checks pass because the vendor is real.

case.headline: Toyota Boshoku lost $37M (2019)
case.detail: Attackers persuaded an employee with financial authority to change the bank details on a transfer.

fact.text: The FBI advises confirming any change to a vendor's bank details through a contact you already have on file, not one given in the email.

title: Look-alike vendor
search_query: business email compromise spoofed domain impersonating legitimate company fraudulent invoices vendors
how: Criminals register a company or web domain with almost the same name as a supplier you already pay, then send invoices from it. A registry search finds a real company, so the check passes.

case.headline: Facebook and Google lost $122M (2013-2015)
case.detail: A scammer set up a company with the same name as Quanta Computer, a real supplier to both, and sent them fake invoices.

fact.text: FBI example of a spoofed domain: @company.com becomes @co-pany.com.

title: Boss pressure and payment bursts
search_query: business email compromise CEO impersonation urgent confidential wire transfer scam warning
how: An urgent, confidential request appears to come from the CEO or CFO, sometimes backed by a call or video meeting. Several large payments go to new payees before anyone double-checks.

case.headline: Arup lost $25M (2024)
case.detail: A Hong Kong employee made 15 transfers to 5 bank accounts after a video call in which every colleague was a deepfake.

fact.text: 74% of US organisations were hit by business email compromise in 2025.

title: Fake, duplicate or inflated invoice
search_query: billing scheme fraud duplicate invoices fictitious invoices accounts payable red flags
how: An invoice arrives for work that never happened, reuses a real invoice number so a second copy slips through, or bills far more than usual. The vendor itself may look fine.

fact.text: Business email compromise cost US businesses $3.05B in 2025, about $123k per complaint, and 86% of it went out by wire or ACH.

title: Insider paying themselves
search_query: employee sentenced embezzlement fictitious vendor shell company fake invoices employer
how: An employee pays a shell company or a relative, keeping each payment just under the amount that needs a second approval.

fact.text: More than half of fraud cases involve missing internal controls or someone overriding them, and the typical scheme runs 12 months before it's caught.
